images.title: The product is a common multiple
images.purpose: Show on a number line that 48, the product of 6 and 8, is a common multiple, and the LCM 24 comes first.
images.composition: One long horizontal number line across the frame with dots above and below, two circled meeting points, and white space above and below.
exact_structure: One grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 48, drawn to an even scale so equal gaps of 6 and equal gaps of 8 look equal, with a tick and the label 0 at the left end and no other tick labels.
Exactly 8 teal #0072B2 dots above the line at 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, with the label multiples of 6 at the left above the line.
Exactly 6 amber #E69F00 dots below the line at 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, with the label multiples of 8 at the left below the line.
Exactly 2 reddish purple #CC79A7 rings around the points 24 and 48, where teal and amber dots meet.
Under the ring at 24 the label LCM = 24; under the ring at 48 the label 6 × 8 = 48.
rejection: more or fewer than 8 teal dots or 6 amber dots, or any dot off its multiple
images.takeaway: The product is always a common multiple, so the lowest common multiple can never be bigger than it.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 48 with multiples of 6 above and of 8 below, meeting at 24 (the LCM) and 48 (the product).
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video comparing the LCM with the product.
images.teaching_notes: Find where the dots first meet, then where they meet again at the product.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the product as a later meeting point on the number line explains why the LCM is never greater.
